BeforeCardPlayed.rationale: ChemicalX.cs:17-29 is a pure presentation hook: two early returns and a Flash() when the played card is the owner's and costs X. It has no model effect whatsoever -- the actual +2 lives in ModifyXValue -- so there is nothing for the sim to drop. RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

ModifyXValue.rationale: ChemicalX.cs:31-38 returns `originalValue + DynamicVars['Increase'].IntValue` (2) for the owner's cards; chemical_x.py:20 returns `value + 2`. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): with 3 energy, playing Cascade gives `energy 3 -> 0, captured_x=5`, i.e. X is raised to 5 while the energy actually spent stays 3 -- the relic's whole point. The sim consults the hook at both X capture sites, the normal play (combat.py:406) and the auto-play (combat.py:549), matching the game's single ResolveEnergyXValue capture.

guards.rationale: The `player != base.Owner` / `card.Owner != base.Owner` / `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player (and, for the participants form, also admits pets). The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState) and models no pet creature, so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

2, with no AscensionHelper call in the file. This is a KEYED DynamicVar ('Increase'), read with the string indexer rather than a typed accessor -- the same idiom relic/bread's N4 records -- so there is no second var to confuse it with.

guards.what: N3: the star-cost half -- `cardPlay.Card.HasStarCostX` (ChemicalX.cs:23) and, through it, ModifyXValue applying to a star X as well as an energy X
guards.rationale: Star cost is the second, parallel cost currency and the sim models no star-cost concept anywhere. Same waiver, same reasoning and the same revisit condition as audit/records/relic/brilliant_scarf.json's TryModifyStarCost: the whole SYSTEM is out of the sim's scope, not merely this relic's use of it, and no ported card carries a star cost. If star costs are ever ported this must be revisited, because C#'s ModifyXValue is currency-agnostic and would raise both.

guards.what: N4: the sim's aggregator clamps the result with `max(0, value)` (hooks.py:261); Hook.ModifyXValue does not (Hook.cs:2071-2079)
guards.rationale: Unobservable with today's content: the base value fed in is the player's current energy, which is never negative (combat.py:406, 549), and the only ported implementer of the hook is this relic, which only ADDS. A ported X-reducer would expose it. Checked rather than skipped because a silent clamp in a chain aggregator is exactly the kind of difference that never shows up in a single-listener test. Rule 7: hooks.py and Hook.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N5: the sim has X-cost cards for the relic to modify
guards.rationale: Binding rule 5 forbids resting on an unexecuted reachability claim in either direction. EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): the ported X-cost cards are ['cascade', 'volley', 'whirlwind'], and Chemical X is Shop rarity in the transcribed grab bag (`batch3-pool`), so the relic and its trigger are both live content. The rollup below is a waiver only because every divergence found is presentation, multiplayer or the absent star-cost currency -- not because the relic is unreachable.
